description:
People care a whole lot less about what you’re doing than you think they do.

Most people are too busy overthinking their own life, their own insecurities, their own problems, their own next move to spend much time judging yours.

Which is actually freeing when you think about it.

The thing you’re scared to post.
The business you’re scared to start.
The boundary you’re scared to set.
The life you secretly want.

Most people aren’t paying nearly as much attention as your fear wants you to believe.

And the ones who are?
Usually aren’t the people building anything meaningful anyway.

Stop making decisions based on imaginary criticism from people who are consumed with themselves.

Go live your life.
transcript: People don't care as much about what you do as you think they do. Everybody cares about themselves. And so many times we're worrying if we fail. We're worrying if it doesn't go good. We're worrying if we embarrass ourselves. In front of who? The most embarrassing thing we could ever do is get to the end of your life and realize you played small. You left all of it on the table and you don't get another shot. That's what could be embarrassing. That's more scary to me than anything else. Getting to the end and realize you freaking missed it.
